excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<parithoshj> From Matty:
individual payload observations are now exposed on The Lab](https://lab.ethpandaops.io/ethereum/execution/payloads (https://lab.ethpandaops.io/ethereum/execution/payloads). Direct linking to the corresponding blocks. Reach out if you've got questions or want help digging into the data.

There's a filter for reference nodes, so we can use this as a way to figure out which exact blocks are bad on reference machines on mainnet and then convert those into new benchmarks and eventually stateful tests.

excerpts.content: <gakonst> What's the most promising EIP to "fix" XEN atm?

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<CPerezz> re: **@gakonst**
> What's the most promising EIP to "fix" XEN atm?
Still pending measurements and tests we are working on atm based on deep branching storage retrieval.

For now 8032 is the best bet. But we still need to confirm some intuitions that otherwise would require refactoring 8032.


Ideal solution would look like: Tree-traversion-based costs.
The problem is that this would mean we have to open the trie and price after which means some stuff in block computation would require heavy refactoring.
